definitions: The quality of something is often directly related to its price; cheaper items may be of lower quality.
It is often worth spending more money to obtain a better quality product or service.
examples: I bought the cheapest shoes, and they fell apart in a month. Well, you get what you pay for.
She decided to go with the more expensive mechanic, knowing that you get what you pay for.
Don't complain about the poor service; you get what you pay for with budget airlines.
lemma: you get what you pay for
source: you get what you pay for
